label: sec:algebraic-substrate-preamble
html:
This section exhibits the algebraic object whose internal geometry generates the physical observations. The quantum vacuum formalises as a self-dual Frobenius--Hopf algebra A living in a rigid monoidal category \mathbf{C}.

The algebra A carries three layers of structure. The Frobenius form \lambda \colon A \to \mathbf{1} and the Hopf comultiplication \Delta \colon A \to A \otimes A endow A with an inner product and a coalgebra structure, related by the Frobenius compatibility condition. A categorical Reeb derivation \xi_q \colon A \to A encodes the observer drift—the intrinsic time evolution generated by the contact structure on the state bundle \mathcal{S}. The spectral geometry of Bring's curve \mathcal{B} provides the coordinate fibers: the 2g = 8 independent cycles of this genus-4 curve determine the fundamental modes of the Reeb spectrum.

Self-duality is the principle that closes the construction. The rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet forms the duality theory for the non-commutative algebra A [yekutieli2010]. The Frobenius form induces a quasi-isomorphism A \xrightarrow{\sim} \omega_A^\bullet, establishing that the observer trace \Phi = \lambda \circ \mu and the observed state space are intrinsically paired. The substrate is simultaneously the algebra of observables and the space on which those observables act.

Algebraic and geometric precedent on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)). Two structural distinctions separate the infinite-dimensional coordinate algebra \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) from the finite-rank Frobenius towers used later in this paper. By the theorem of Richard G. Larson and Moss E. Sweedler [larson-sweedler1969], every finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field carries a Frobenius form supplied by a nonzero integral; conversely, Bertrand I-peng Lin [lin1977] proved that an infinite-dimensional coalgebra or Hopf algebra admits no nonzero integral of finite dual rank, so \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) as a whole is not a unital Frobenius algebra. Infinite-dimensional group and quantum-group coordinate algebras instead form multiplier Hopf algebras in the sense of Alfons Van Daele [vandaele1994], or nonunital and H^*-Frobenius structures in the infinite-dimensional categorical quantum mechanics of Samson Abramsky and Chris Heunen [abramsky-heunen2012]. In this paper, genuine Frobenius objects enter only at finite rank: either on finite-dimensional truncations or along the finite-level Iwahori--Hecke and Temperley--Lieb centralizer tower, which forms a tower of Frobenius extensions in the sense of Lars Kadison [kadison1999] whose convention-D Markov trace has subfactor index [2]_q^2 \ge 4 in the positive range of Vaughan F. R. Jones [jones1983]. Moreover, on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) at q \neq \pm 1, the Haar state constructed by Stanisław Lech Woronowicz [woronowicz1987] is non-tracial and carries a nontrivial modular automorphism \vartheta satisfying h(ab) = h(b\,\vartheta(a)); that modular automorphism of the coordinate algebra is not the Nakayama twist of the finite Iwahori--Hecke / Temperley--Lieb tower, where the Markov trace on the semisimple Temperley--Lieb quotient is symmetric (\mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx)) and the tower therefore has trivial Nakayama automorphism \nu = \mathrm{id}.

The differential, bundle, and Hodge ingredients assembled on the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) model likewise rest on established noncommutative geometry. Woronowicz constructed the three-dimensional left-covariant differential calculus on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) [woronowicz1987-twisted-su2] and the general theory of bicovariant differential calculi on compact matrix pseudogroups [woronowicz1989], while Piotr Stachura [stachura1992] and Konrad Schmüdgen and Axel Schüler [schmudgen-schuler1995] classified the four-dimensional bicovariant calculi on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) and \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}(N)). Over the quantum two-spheres introduced by Piotr Podleś [podles1987], Tomasz Brzeziński and Shahn Majid [brzezinski-majid1993] developed quantum principal bundles and the q-monopole connection, Shahn Majid [majid1995, majid2002, majid2005] formulated braided and noncommutative Riemannian and spin geometry on the standard q-sphere, Réamonn Ó Buachalla [obuachalla2016] constructed noncommutative complex structures on quantum homogeneous spaces, Giovanni Landi and Alessandro Zampini [landi-zampini2011] studied differential calculi, Hodge operators, and Laplacians on the quantum Hopf fibration, and Partha Sarathi Chakraborty and Arupkumar Pal [chakraborty-pal2003] together with Ludwik Dąbrowski, Giovanni Landi, Andrzej Sitarz, Walter van Suijlekom, and Joseph C. Várilly [dabrowski-landi-sitarz-vansuijlekom-varilly2005] constructed equivariant spectral triples and the Dirac operator on \mathrm{SU}_q(2). No new differential calculus on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is claimed here; the chapter organises the three-dimensional left-covariant contact and Reeb datum into the categorical action functional used downstream.
